title: You have been caught in a lie
lede: It was small, or it started small. Now the person is holding it, looking at you, and the next thirty seconds decide whether this is something you recover from or the beginning of a much longer problem. The reflex is to explain. The reflex is wrong.

blocks.text: It was small, or it started small. Now the person is holding it, looking at you, and the next thirty seconds decide whether this is something you recover from or the beginning of a much longer problem. The reflex is to explain. The reflex is wrong.

items: The damage is not the content of the lie. It is that they now have to re-examine everything else you have said, and that is the actual work you have created for them.
A second lie to protect the first is the moment recoverable becomes unrecoverable. Almost everyone attempts it, and it is what turns an incident into a character judgement.
You cannot argue your way back to being trusted. Trust is rebuilt by a period of verifiable behaviour, on their timeline, and the only thing you control today is whether you tell the whole truth now.

items.detail: In the first sentence, without qualification. Every second of hedging is more expensive than the original lie, and partial admissions are read as further deception.

items.move: Volunteer the rest before they find it
items.detail: If there is more, say it now. The single most damaging pattern is a series of admissions extracted one at a time over weeks.
Reasons offered in the same breath as an admission are heard as excuses. Say what you did, say it was wrong, and stop.
Show that you understand the real injury — that they now have to doubt other things. This is what distinguishes a real admission from a managed one.
Something checkable, not "I would never again". Access, transparency, a specific change they can observe.

items.move: Accept their timeline without negotiating it
items.detail: Do not ask when things will be normal. Asking for a schedule for forgiveness is the last move of someone managing an image.

items.say: "You are right. I lied about it. I am not going to try to make that sound better than it is."
"Before you find out from somewhere else — there are two other things I have not been straight about."
"I know the problem is not just this. It is that you now have to wonder about other things I have told you."
"I am not asking you to take my word for it. Here is what you can see for yourself."
"I can tell you why, if it helps. But I want to be clear it is an explanation, not a defence."
"I am not going to ask you to be okay with this yet. Take whatever time you need."

items: Minimising the size of it. Arguing about how bad the lie was tells them you are still managing the story rather than telling the truth.
Explaining your reasons first. It lands as justification and the admission stops counting.
Adding a second lie to hold up the first. This is the exact point at which a recoverable situation becomes a permanent one.
Pointing out something they have done. The moment you introduce a comparison, you have chosen a fight over a repair.
Demanding to know how they found out. It shows your attention is on the leak rather than on the lie, and everyone notices.
Expect to be checked, and be gracious about it every time. Impatience with verification is how people lose the second chance they were given.
Work out honestly what the lie was protecting — embarrassment, an argument you did not want, a version of yourself. That is the thing to change.
If it involved other people, tell them plainly too, before it reaches them sideways.
Do not perform remorse. Sustained ordinary honesty is more convincing than any amount of visible suffering.
Accept that some relationships end here and that the apology was still the right thing to do.

limit: If the lie has legal, financial, professional or regulatory consequences — a false statement to an employer, an insurer, a court or a regulator — take advice before making a written admission. Being honest with a person and formally admitting a liability are different acts, and doing the second without advice can remove protections you may need.
